sources.title: Rehabilitation and Return to Sports after Achilles Tendon Repair
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Marrone W, Andrews R, Reynolds A, et al.
sources.population: Adults after surgical Achilles tendon repair; recommendations synthesize literature and clinical practice.
sources.limitations: Not a trial or a surgeon-specific protocol. Exercise timing, loading and return-to-sport decisions still require individual assessment; cited healthy-adult biomechanics are indirect.

sources.title: Return to running after Achilles tendon rupture: an international Delphi consensus
sources.population: Return-to-running decisions after Achilles tendon rupture.
sources.limitations: Consensus criteria require prospective validation and do not make a single exercise, elapsed time or 90% symmetry a universal clearance rule.

sources.title: Achilles Tendon Loading During Heel-Raising and -Lowering Exercises
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Revak A, Diers K, Kernozek TW
sources.population: Healthy younger adults performing heel-raise and heel-lowering variations.
sources.limitations: Estimates relative tendon loading; it does not establish postoperative readiness, safety, dose, range or progression timing.
sources.developerCorrection: Author list corrected from original PMC article.

sources.title: Human Achilles tendon adaptation in response to exercise: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.population: Primarily healthy participants in tendon-loading studies.
sources.limitations: General tendon adaptation evidence is not a postoperative prescription and does not validate any candidate's starting load or eligibility.

sources.title: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.authorsOrOrganization: American College of Sports Medicine; Currier and colleagues
sources.limitations: Supports general resistance-training principles only; not Achilles repair clearance, exercise-specific dosing, or equivalence among machines and free weights.

sources.title: Effects of short foot training on foot posture in patients with flatfeet: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.population: People with flat feet; studies varied in symptoms and intervention duration.
sources.limitations: Indirect to surgically repaired Achilles tendons; does not show that this drill is required, safe now, or superior to current rehabilitation.
sources.developerVerification: Title reconciled; PMID pairing still requires verification.

sources.title: Effects of backward walking exercise on knee osteoarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
sources.evidenceType: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
sources.limitations: Wrong clinical population for postoperative Achilles decisions; does not verify treadmill compatibility or establish a safe speed, grade, dose or progression.

sources.title: Mammoth Belt Squat product page
sources.population: Equipment users; not a clinical population.
sources.limitations: Supports only advertised equipment use. It is not clinical evidence, does not confirm the user's exact attachment/configuration, and does not confer readiness.

sources.title: Foot and Ankle Conditioning Program
sources.population: General foot and ankle conditioning audience.
sources.limitations: Generic instruction, not a postoperative Achilles protocol, individualized clearance or validation of candidate-specific loading.

sources.title: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
sources.limitations: Technique reference only; not specific to a trap bar, Smith machine, surgical Achilles rehabilitation, or personalized loading.

candidates.name: Tibialis raise
candidates.decisionReason: No exact record was found. Add as optional anterior lower-leg reference content, not as an Achilles progression criterion.
candidates.purpose: Anterior lower-leg strength and ankle dorsiflexion control.
setupSteps: Stand with upper back against a wall and feet slightly forward.
Keep heels planted and begin with toes relaxed on the floor.
executionCues: Lift the forefeet toward the shins without rocking onto the heels.
Lower under control while the heels stay down.
commonErrors: Bending the knees to create the motion.
Rocking the whole body instead of moving at the ankles.
Letting the feet roll outward.
candidates.loadConvention: Bodyweight; record no numeric load unless an independently reviewed resistance setup is used.
achillesConsiderations: Catalog inclusion does not establish current tolerance for repeated ankle motion.
Stop and apply the existing symptom/red-flag process if symptoms change.
unresolvedPrerequisites: Current ankle range and symptom response are not supplied.
